corrections.text: The summary says the organizations handled AI-found vulnerabilities differently "in October". Several of the developments predate October: the GNOME bug bounty received its final report on February 23, 2026 and was announced as ended in Catanzaro's October 2 post; The Hacker News says the kernel security documentation was updated in May 2026; and GNOME Security's 30-day disclosure deadline took effect August 1. Google's pause took effect October 1.

The article cites Catanzaro's GNOME CVE counts (13 for 2023, 141 for 2026 through September 30) and his statement that AI is "the primary cause for the increase". His post counts CVEs by the year an issue was reported, says the data is accurate through roughly September 1, and adds that AI "is not the only reason" because GNOME maintainers also got better at flagging issues for security tracking.
